A missing component, delayed delivery or unreliable supplier can directly impact production. As an Operational Buyer, you will take responsibility for the operational purchasing process and the availability of materials and components. Suppliers and commercial agreements are already in place; your focus is on making sure purchase orders are executed correctly, deliveries arrive as promised and potential supply issues are addressed before they impact the factory. This is a hands-on role where you will be in direct contact with suppliers and work closely with planning, manufacturing and logistics. You will monitor the supply situation, manage changing priorities and take ownership when deliveries or material availability are at risk. Your work will include: Managing and following up on purchase orders for technical materials and components. Monitoring delivery performance and acting when suppliers are at risk of missing agreed lead times. Maintaining direct contact with suppliers regarding order status, delays and delivery commitments. Coordinating material availability with planning and manufacturing teams. Taking ownership of shortages, supply disruptions and other operational issues until they are resolved. Escalating critical supply issues and coordinating actions with the right internal and external stakeholders. Making operational purchasing decisions based on lead times, delivery requirements and costs. Identifying recurring supply issues and contributing to structural improvements. Maintaining accurate purchasing and material data in SAP or another ERP system. Experience managing purchase orders and working directly with suppliers. Experience within a technical, manufacturing or industrial environment. The ability to manage multiple priorities and remain structured when circumstances change. A proactive mindset and a strong sense of ownership. The confidence to challenge suppliers and escalate issues when necessary. Experience with SAP or another ERP system. Good communication skills and a strong command of English. Location: The Netherlands | Full-time | Open to candidates currently based in Spain Are you experienced in Revit or BIM and interested in moving your career into the high-voltage and energy infrastructure sector? As an Electrical BIM Modeler, you will work on the design and development of high-voltage substations in the Netherlands. You will translate electrical engineering input into accurate 3D models and technical drawings, working closely with Primary and Secondary Engineers, Civil Engineers and other BIM specialists. You will work on both new substations and extensions or modifications of existing installations. What will you do? You will be responsible for developing and maintaining BIM models for electrical substation projects. Your work will include: Creating and updating 3D BIM models for high-voltage substations; Modelling electrical equipment and substation components in Autodesk Revit; Working with equipment such as transformers, circuit breakers, disconnectors, busbars, cable routes and supporting structures; Producing layouts, sections, details and technical drawings from the 3D model; Adding and maintaining technical information and object data within the BIM environment; Coordinating the electrical model with Civil, Structural and other engineering disciplines; Identifying clashes and design inconsistencies; Processing design changes throughout different project phases; Supporting Primary and Secondary Engineers with model-based engineering; Contributing to BIM standards, libraries and modelling workflows; Checking models and drawings for quality, completeness and constructability. Arbeidsvoorwaarden €3,500 – €4,500 gross per month, depending on experience; 22 vacation days + 13 ATV days: 35 days off per year; Hybrid working possibilities and a home-working allowance; Commuting allowance or business public-transport card; A strong pension scheme; Technical and personal development through professional training; Opportunities to develop towards SeniBIM Modeler, BIM Coordinator or Electrical Engineering; Bicycle leasing and fitness schemes; International and multidisciplinary engineering projects; A professional but informal working environment. Why move from Spain to the Netherlands? The Netherlands is investing heavily in the expansion and reinforcement of its electricity grid. This creates long-term engineering opportunities in substations and high-voltage infrastructure. For an experienced electrical BIM professional, this role offers the opportunity to develop specialist knowledge in a sector with a substantial long-term project pipeline. Functie-eisen We are interested in candidates with either an engineering or technical vocational background. Relevant Spanish qualifications include, for example: Grado en Ingeniería Eléctrica; Grado en Ingeniería Electrónica Industrial y Automática; Grado en Ingeniería en Tecnologías Industriales; Técnico Superior en Proyectos de Sistemas Electrotécnicos y Automatizados (CFGS); Older Ingeniero Técnico Industrial qualifications; Or another relevant electrical, industrial or technical qualification.
